title: U.S. data-centre use and grid growth
description: Compare estimated growth in data-centre electricity use with U.S. electricity sales and summer generating capacity.
plainLanguageSummary: From 2020 to 2024, data-centre electricity use rose 82.9%, electricity sales 6.9%, and summer generating capacity 18.2%.
howToRead: All three lines start at 100 in 2020. The index compares growth rates and does not put their very different absolute scales on one axis.

calculation.formula: Each series is indexed to its 2020 value = 100 using the presentation's source table.
calculation.explanation: The index compares rates of change; absolute TWh and the LBNL 2030 cases appear in the separate scale-comparator chart.
calculation.example: An index value of 150 means the series is 50% above its 2020 level.

patternsToWatch: The difference between estimated data-centre use and total electricity growth
Whether new capacity growth catches up with large-load demand
limitations: Data-centre energy values are estimates and include non-AI uses.
National annual totals do not identify regional interconnection capacity or local grid constraints.
The 2020–2024 historical comparison is separate from the published 2030 demand scenarios.
sourceNotes: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory data-centre usage reports
U.S. Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Annual, annual electricity sales and summer capacity
